Definition: the cheek (from its fleshiness); hence, the jaw-bone
BiblicalUsage: Lechi the word is the cheek, and the jawbone — the part of the face that takes the blow, and the bone Samson fought with. In Judges 15:15, "And he found a new jawbone of an ass"; and in 1 Kings 22:24, "and smote Micaiah on the cheek". In Hosea 11:4, "with bands of love: and I was to them as they that take off the yoke on their jaws"; and in Lamentations 3:30, "He giveth [his] cheek to him that smiteth him: he is filled full with reproach.".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the cheek is where humility is tested — the prophet is smitten for speaking truth, and the Lord says to turn the other cheek. I hold that Samson's jawbone won a battle, but God's yoke lifted from the jaws is the greater mercy. My position is that I would rather be smitten for truth than strike back in anger.
